import sys, json, uuid, datetime, hashlib, re

# GH #138 (ruling R-0904-6) -- this cell's page bounds are PARAMS, not
# environment. The incoming message and this cell's own configuration arrive on
# the same stdin document: `params` is one of its three top-level objects,
# beside `envelope` and `body`, and the substrate always sets it ({} when there
# is nothing to hand over). So the bound is per-INSTANCE -- two registries in
# one colony page apart, and a mutation retunes one of them without touching a
# colony-wide environment. The literal beside each name is the shipped default,
# and it is the same number `contract.settings` declares.


def _knob(key, default):
    # A knob explicitly set to null or to whitespace is "not configured", not a
    # crash: an operator who blanks a line in a config means the default.
    v = P.get(key, default)
    return default if v is None else v


def _int(key, default):
    v = _knob(key, default)
    if isinstance(v, str) and not v.strip():
        return default
    return int(v)


# GH #855 -- the ops this hand takes on `in_hand`. `remap` moves a tier (what it
# always did); the other five are the registry as the ONE way to operate models:
# a replacement set and cleared, a cell put back on what it resolves to without
# one, the view per cell, and the row that makes a cell a subscriber at all.
# GH #858 adds three: the operator keeps the catalogue (`model_upsert`,
# `model_retire`) on the same lane, with the same actor, instead of over a
# boot-graph edge nobody at run time has, and `retranslate` runs the
# translations a failed translator left missing.
OPS = ("remap", "override_set", "override_clear", "reset", "show", "subscribe",
       "model_upsert", "model_retire", "retranslate")

# GH #853 -- the keys of a model package, in the order the llm cell names them
# (`MODEL_PACKAGE_KEYS` in crates/meclaw-cells/src/llm/params.rs). A push sets
# the keys the resolved package carries and RESETS every other one, so no key
# of an earlier package survives a model change. A template test compares this
# literal with the Rust constant, so the two cannot drift apart.
MODEL_PACKAGE_KEYS = ["model", "base_url", "wire_dialect", "reasoning_effort",
                      "reasoning_wire", "reasoning", "thinking_budget",
                      "max_tokens", "temperature", "external_timeout_ms",
                      "provider_extra", "model_prompt"]
# Three of them are catalogue COLUMNS, and `model_prompt` is the `prompt`
# column: the `package` json of a row carries the rest and nothing else.
COLUMN_KEYS = ("model", "base_url", "wire_dialect", "model_prompt")
PACKAGE_JSON_KEYS = [k for k in MODEL_PACKAGE_KEYS if k not in COLUMN_KEYS]

# The precedence, highest first. One literal, published in the README table and
# stamped on every resolution: targeted > global > prose > tier > start value.
# `prose` (GH #858) and `tier` never meet on one subscriber: a subscriber that
# states a requirement is resolved by its translation and never by a tier.
RANKS = ("target", "global", "prose", "tier", "start")

# GH #858 -- a requirement is prose, and the llm cell caps its param at the
# same size (`REQUIREMENT_MAX_BYTES` in crates/meclaw-cells/src/llm/params.rs).
REQUIREMENT_MAX_BYTES = 2048

# GH #858 -- a catalogue row as `model_upsert` takes it: every column but the
# id, with the type the store column has. Anything else in the command is
# refused by name rather than dropped, so a typo is not a silent no-op.
MODEL_FIELDS = {"provider": str, "base_url": str, "wire_dialect": str,
                "context_window": int, "cost_in": int, "cost_out": int,
                "caps": dict, "traits": dict, "strengths": str, "status": str,
                "note": str, "package": dict, "prompt": str}
MODEL_STATUSES = ("active", "retired")
MODEL_COLUMNS = ["model_id"] + sorted(MODEL_FIELDS)

# GH #858 -- what the translator is shown of each ACTIVE row, and therefore
# what the catalogue hash covers: a change here is a change of the question.
# Not the endpoint, the package or the prompt block -- they say how to run a
# model once it is chosen, not whether it fits a need -- and not the note.
CATALOGUE_VIEW = ("model_id", "provider", "context_window", "cost_in", "cost_out",
                  "caps", "traits", "strengths")

# The ops that translate what they find untranslated. Everything else reads
# the translations and never asks for one (the plan's "only on change").
ASKING = ("subscribe", "model_upsert", "model_retire", "retranslate")

# The instructions of the translator. They travel in the request's `system`
# slot as the leaf `instructions` (`{"text": ...}`, the leaf form the llm cell
# concatenates), so the translate cell's own config stays a plain llm cell.
TRANSLATOR_INSTRUCTIONS = (
    "You choose one model for one cell of a software system. You are given what the "
    "cell needs, in prose, and a catalogue of models, one JSON object per line: id, "
    "provider, context window in tokens, input and output price in cents per million "
    "tokens, capabilities, curated traits, and strengths in prose. Choose the model "
    "that meets the need fully at the lowest price; when two fit equally, prefer the "
    "one whose strengths match the need more closely. Choose ONLY an id that appears "
    "in the catalogue. Answer with one JSON object and nothing else: "
    "{\"model_id\": \"<an id from the catalogue>\", \"reason\": \"<one sentence>\"}.")

# The longest reason a translation keeps. One sentence is asked for; a model
# that writes a page is cut, not refused -- the choice is what is checked. It
# is kept on ONE line (review of the strand, m-5): `show` hands it to whoever
# reads the view, an agent among them, and a line break or a control
# character in it is the translator writing structure into that view.
REASON_MAX_CHARS = 400

# Review of the strand, m-3: what `model_upsert` takes, bounded where a
# neighbour already bounds it, and REFUSED past the bound, never cut. The
# prompt block: every brain refuses a `model_prompt` over the llm cell's
# `MODEL_PROMPT_MAX_BYTES` (8 KiB) when it is pushed, so a longer one would
# stand in `show` as sent while every cell kept its old params. Strengths ride
# along in EVERY question to the translator, so they are held to the size of
# a requirement. An id is one token of a provider's list -- `vendor/model`,
# with `.`, `:`, `@`, `+`, `-` -- at most 128 characters.
MODEL_PROMPT_MAX_BYTES = 8 * 1024
STRENGTHS_MAX_BYTES = 2 * 1024
MODEL_ID_MAX_CHARS = 128
MODEL_ID_FORM = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:/@+-]*")

# Review of the strand, I-1: a question is written down as OPEN in the same
# bundle that asks it, and an open question is not asked a second time. It
# stays open for this long and no longer: longer than the translate cell's
# backstop (`message_timeout` 90 000 ms, the llm call itself at most 60 000),
# so a question alone in the translator's mailbox is answered or failed by
# then. The backstop bounds one call, not the wait in the mailbox (review
# rev2-L2b1, m-B): of several questions queued behind each other a late one
# can outlive its claim, and a trigger in that window asks it a second time.
# That costs one call and changes no result -- the second answer finds the
# first one's row and is journalled `translation_duplicate`. A template test
# holds this above the backstop.
OPEN_QUESTION_SECONDS = 120

# What `show` says as `because` while a changed requirement holds the prose
# model of the old one (review rev2-L2b1, m-D).
HELD_BECAUSE = "held until the new requirement is answered"


def one_line(v, limit):
    """Text for a view or a journal line: every control character and line
    break a space, runs of spaces one, at most `limit` characters."""
    text = "".join(c if c.isprintable() else " " for c in str(v or ""))
    return " ".join(text.split())[:limit]


def open_cutoff():
    """The oldest `at` an open question may carry and still count as open."""
    t = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc) - datetime.timedelta(
        seconds=OPEN_QUESTION_SECONDS)
    return t.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")


def now():
    return datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")


def emit(route, phase, carry, extra, body=None):
    h = {"route": route, "phase": phase,
         "carry": json.dumps(carry) if carry else "",
         "subscriber": "", "tier": "", "model_id": "", "rank": "",
         "outcome": "", "reason_code": ""}
    h.update(extra or {})
    m = {"header": h}
    m.update(body or {})
    return m


def call(operation, **rest):
    args = {"operation": operation}
    args.update(rest)
    return {"origin": "assistant", "type": "tool_call",
            "id": uuid.uuid4().hex[:12], "text": json.dumps(args)}


def store_bundle(phase, carry, calls):
    """ONE message to the store, one `tool_call` turn per op (GH #295).

    Two or more turns are a bundle and come back as ONE reply with one
    `tool_result` per op in call order -- which is what lets a lane read the
    whole catalogue in one round trip and write everything it decided in one
    more, instead of a python process per row.
    """
    return emit("rstore", phase, carry, None, {"messages": calls})


def fail(detail):
    return emit("error", "", None, {}, {
        "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": "",
                      "text": "llm-registry/hand: " + detail}]})


def ack(cmd, outcome, reason_code, extra):
    payload = {"outcome": outcome, "reason_code": reason_code, "op": cmd.get("op", ""),
               "tier": cmd.get("tier", ""), "model_id": cmd.get("model_id", ""),
               "decided_by": cmd.get("actor", "")}
    payload.update(extra or {})
    return emit("ack", "", None,
                {"outcome": outcome, "reason_code": reason_code,
                 "tier": cmd.get("tier", ""), "model_id": cmd.get("model_id", "")},
                {"messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result",
                               "id": cmd.get("call_id", ""),
                               "text": json.dumps(payload)}]})


def refuse(cmd, reason_code, extra=None):
    """A refusal is acknowledged AND journalled, and changes nothing else."""
    out = []
    if not cmd.get("announce") and not cmd.get("internal"):
        out.append(ack(cmd, "rejected", reason_code, extra))
    out.append(store_bundle("written", None, [journal_call(cmd, cmd.get("cell_path", ""),
                                                          reason_code, "", "")]))
    return out


def journal_call(cmd, cell_path, reason, rank, source_id, model_id=None):
    # The model id of a journal line is on one line and short (review of the
    # strand, m-5): a refused translator answer or a refused upsert is exactly
    # the text nobody vetted.
    mid = cmd.get("model_id", "") if model_id is None else model_id
    return call("insert", table="resolutions", row={
        "id": uuid.uuid4().hex, "tier": cmd.get("tier", ""),
        "model_id": one_line(mid, MODEL_ID_MAX_CHARS),
        "cell_path": cell_path, "at": now(), "reason": reason,
        "rank": rank, "source_id": source_id})


def results_of(d):
    """Every `tool_result` turn of a store reply, parsed, in call order."""
    out = []
    for m in d.get("messages") or []:
        try:
            v = json.loads(m.get("text") or "null")
        except Exception:
            v = None
        out.append(v if isinstance(v, list) else [])
    return out


def as_int(v, fallback=0):
    try:
        return int(v)
    except Exception:
        return fallback


def as_obj(v):
    if isinstance(v, dict):
        return v
    if isinstance(v, str) and v.strip():
        try:
            o = json.loads(v)
        except Exception:
            return {}
        return o if isinstance(o, dict) else {}
    return {}


def first_row(rows):
    for r in rows or []:
        if isinstance(r, dict):
            return r
    return None


def under(path, prefix):
    """A path prefix on SEGMENT boundaries: `/a/talky` covers `/a/talky/brain`
    and `/a/talky` itself, and never `/a/talky-chat/brain`."""
    p = prefix.rstrip("/")
    return bool(p) and (path == p or path.startswith(p + "/"))


def digest(value):
    return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"),
                                     ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:16]


# --- GH #858: the requirement and the catalogue, as the two halves of a key --


def requirement_of(v):
    """(text, ok) for a requirement as a command or an announcement states it.

    Stripped, because two templates that differ in a trailing newline state the
    same need; bounded like the llm param it mirrors. Not a string, or too long,
    is not ok -- and "" is a statement too: this cell states no requirement.
    """
    if not isinstance(v, str):
        return "", False
    text = v.strip()
    if len(text.encode("utf-8")) > REQUIREMENT_MAX_BYTES:
        return "", False
    return text, True


def requirement_hash(text):
    """sha256[:16] of the requirement, "" for none -- the llm cell's stderr line
    shows the first 8 of the same digest, so a row and a cell can be matched."""
    return hashlib.sha256(text.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:16] if text else ""


def catalogue_rows(world):
    """What the translator is shown: every ACTIVE row, CATALOGUE_VIEW only,
    normalised, in `model_id` order."""
    out = []
    for model_id in sorted(world["models"]):
        r = world["models"][model_id]
        out.append({"model_id": model_id,
                    "provider": str(r.get("provider") or ""),
                    "context_window": as_int(r.get("context_window"), 0),
                    "cost_in": as_int(r.get("cost_in"), 0),
                    "cost_out": as_int(r.get("cost_out"), 0),
                    "caps": as_obj(r.get("caps")),
                    "traits": as_obj(r.get("traits")),
                    "strengths": str(r.get("strengths") or "")})
    return out


def catalogue_hash(world):
    """The catalogue half of a translation's key. Same active rows, same view,
    same hash -- a price change or a retired model is a new question, a new
    prompt block for a model is not."""
    return digest(catalogue_rows(world))


# --- the resolution: ONE deterministic function (OR-SN-48) -------------------
#
# It reads five tables and nothing else -- `models`, `tiers`, `overrides`,
# `subscribers` and, since GH #858, `translations` -- and the same five tables
# resolve the same subscriber the same way every time. No clock, no model, no
# order the store happened to return rows in: every tie is broken by a literal
# key. The translator never runs in here: its answer is a ROW, written once per
# (requirement, catalogue) and read like any other.

def base_of(sub, world):
    """(model, rank, source, because) a global replacement is compared with.

    With a requirement: its translation -- a tier is not consulted while one
    stands, because the cell said in prose what it needs. While there is none
    (a new or changed requirement not answered yet, a translator that failed,
    an answer refused), the cell keeps the PROSE model it holds, if that model
    is still active (review of the strand, I-2): no `$reset`, no detour
    through the start value, and never an empty model for a cell born on an
    empty key. Nothing held: the tier's model, else the start value -- the
    same as without a requirement (0.46.0 unchanged). Deterministic all the
    same: what a cell holds is a column of `subscribers`. Never the model a
    replacement already put there -- a global `X -> Y` beside a global
    `Y -> Z` is two statements, not a chain.
    """
    start = str(sub.get("start_model") or "")
    rh = str(sub.get("requirement_hash") or "")
    if rh:
        t = world["prose"].get(rh)
        if t:
            return t["model_id"], "prose", "translation:" + rh, t["reason"]
        held = str(sub.get("base_model") or "")
        if str(sub.get("base_rank") or "") == "prose" and held in world["models"]:
            return (held, "prose", str(sub.get("base_source") or ""),
                    str(sub.get("because") or ""))
    tier = str(sub.get("tier") or "")
    trow = world["tiers"].get(tier) if tier else None
    if trow:
        return str(trow.get("model_id") or ""), "tier", "tier:" + tier, ""
    return start, "start", "", ""


def resolve(sub, world):
    """(rank, model_id, source_id, reason, because) for one subscriber row.

    `because` is the translator's sentence for the BASE, whatever rank wins
    on top of it: a subscriber row keeps its base (`base_model`, `base_rank`,
    `base_source`, `because`) so that the base can be held while a new
    question is open, also under a replacement. `view` shows the sentence
    only while the rank is `prose`.
    """
    active = world["models"]
    path = str(sub.get("cell_path") or "")
    start = str(sub.get("start_model") or "")
    pinned = as_int(sub.get("pinned"), 0) == 1
    cands = []
    # targeted: the LONGEST path prefix wins, the newest row breaks a tie, the
    # id breaks the next one. It reaches a pinned subscriber too -- a targeted
    # replacement is the operator's statement about exactly this cell, and a pin
    # is a statement about everything that is NOT addressed at it.
    targets = [o for o in world["overrides"]
               if o.get("scope") == "target" and under(path, str(o.get("match") or ""))]
    if targets:
        best = max(targets, key=lambda o: (len(str(o.get("match") or "").rstrip("/")),
                                           str(o.get("since") or ""), str(o.get("id") or "")))
        cands.append(("target", str(best.get("model_id") or ""), str(best.get("id") or ""),
                      "override_target"))
    base, base_rank, base_src, because = base_of(sub, world)
    if not pinned:
        # global: "model X everywhere -> Y" replaces the BASE model, whatever
        # put it there -- a translation, a tier or the start value.
        globals_ = [o for o in world["overrides"]
                    if o.get("scope") == "global" and str(o.get("match") or "") == base]
        if globals_:
            g = sorted(globals_, key=lambda o: (str(o.get("since") or ""),
                                                str(o.get("id") or "")))[-1]
            cands.append(("global", str(g.get("model_id") or ""), str(g.get("id") or ""),
                          "override_global"))
        if base_rank == "prose":
            cands.append(("prose", base, base_src, "prose_translated"))
        if base_rank == "tier":
            cands.append(("tier", base, base_src, "tier_active"))
    held = {"base_model": base if base_rank == "prose" else "",
            "base_rank": base_rank if base_rank == "prose" else "",
            "base_source": base_src if base_rank == "prose" else "",
            "because": because if base_rank == "prose" else ""}
    for rank, model_id, source_id, reason in cands:
        # A model the catalogue does not carry as active is no resolution: it
        # has no package, and pushing a name without one would move a cell onto
        # something nobody described. The next rank decides instead.
        if model_id in active:
            return rank, model_id, source_id, reason, held
    return "start", start, "", "start_value", held


def package_of(model_id, world):
    """The params a push sets, from one catalogue row. Empty values are unset."""
    row = world["models"].get(model_id) or {}
    out = {"model": model_id}
    for key, col in (("base_url", "base_url"), ("wire_dialect", "wire_dialect")):
        v = row.get(col)
        if isinstance(v, str) and v.strip():
            out[key] = v
    pkg = as_obj(row.get("package"))
    for k in PACKAGE_JSON_KEYS:
        if k in pkg and pkg[k] is not None and pkg[k] != "":
            out[k] = pkg[k]
    prompt = row.get("prompt")
    if isinstance(prompt, str) and prompt.strip():
        out["model_prompt"] = prompt
    return out


def push_params(rank, model_id, world):
    """The params slot of a push -- the WHOLE package plus `$reset` for the rest.

    A start value is never pushed as a value: the cell already holds it, in its
    own birth params, so falling back to it is a reset of every package key.
    """
    if rank == "start":
        return {"$reset": list(MODEL_PACKAGE_KEYS)}
    pkg = package_of(model_id, world)
    pkg["$reset"] = [k for k in MODEL_PACKAGE_KEYS if k not in pkg]
    return pkg


def package_hash(rank, params):
    """What was pushed, as 16 hex chars; the start value is the EMPTY hash.

    Empty because a subscriber row starts empty: a cell that was never pushed
    and resolves to its start value has nothing to be told, and a cell that was
    pushed and falls back has a hash that is not empty -- which is exactly the
    one case that needs a `$reset`.
    """
    if rank == "start":
        return ""
    return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(params, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))
                          .encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:16]


def push(cell_path, tier, rank, model_id, params):
    """The one wire an `llm` cell understands for a model change.

    A PARAMS-ONLY body: an EMPTY `system` slot and no `messages`. The llm cell
    takes package keys only from a body without a `messages` slot (GH #853),
    merges them into its live params, persists them in its own cell.db and
    emits nothing -- no inference, no provider call, no cost. The empty system
    slot is not decoration: a message body has to carry `system`, `messages`
    or `attachments` (ubf-body.json), and a body carrying only `params` is
    dead-lettered as an invalid body before it reaches the cell.
    """
    return emit("update", "", None,
                {"subscriber": cell_path, "tier": tier, "model_id": model_id,
                 "rank": rank},
                {"system": {}, "params": params})


def settle(cmd, subs, world, reason_push, reason_pinned, touched):
    """Resolve every subscriber in `subs`; push and record the ones that moved.

    Returns (writes, pushes, counts). `touched` says which subscribers the op
    could have moved at all, so a pinned one that a tier or global change
    passed over is journalled as skipped rather than silently left out.
    """
    writes, pushes = [], []
    counts = {"pushed": 0, "unchanged": 0, "skipped_pinned": 0}
    stamp = now()
    for s in subs:
        path = str(s.get("cell_path") or "")
        if not path:
            continue
        rank, model_id, source_id, reason, held = resolve(s, world)
        params = push_params(rank, model_id, world)
        h = package_hash(rank, params)
        old = str(s.get("package_hash") or "")
        state = {"model_id": model_id, "rank": rank, "reason": reason}
        state.update(held)
        if h != old:
            pushes.append(push(path, str(s.get("tier") or ""), rank, model_id, params))
            state.update({"package_hash": h, "since": stamp})
            writes.append(call("update", table="subscribers", set=state,
                               where={"cell_path": path}))
            writes.append(journal_call(cmd, path, reason_push, rank, source_id, model_id))
            counts["pushed"] += 1
            continue
        if (str(s.get("model_id") or "") != model_id or str(s.get("rank") or "") != rank
                or str(s.get("reason") or "") != reason
                or any(str(s.get(k) or "") != v for k, v in held.items())):
            # Same bytes on the wire, a different reason for them: the view is
            # corrected and nothing is sent, because the cell runs it already.
            writes.append(call("update", table="subscribers", set=state,
                               where={"cell_path": path}))
        if as_int(s.get("pinned"), 0) == 1 and touched(s) and rank != "target":
            writes.append(journal_call(cmd, path, reason_pinned, rank, source_id, model_id))
            counts["skipped_pinned"] += 1
        else:
            counts["unchanged"] += 1
    return writes, pushes, counts


def world_of(results):
    models_rows, tier_rows, override_rows, sub_rows = (results + [[], [], [], []])[:4]
    return {
        "models": {str(r.get("model_id") or ""): r for r in models_rows
                   if isinstance(r, dict) and r.get("model_id")},
        "tiers": {str(r.get("tier") or ""): r for r in tier_rows
                  if isinstance(r, dict) and r.get("tier")},
        "overrides": [r for r in override_rows if isinstance(r, dict)],
        "subs": [r for r in sub_rows if isinstance(r, dict)],
        "prose": {},
    }


SUBSCRIBER_COLUMNS = ["cell_path", "tier", "pinned", "start_model", "package_hash",
                      "model_id", "rank", "reason", "since", "requirement",
                      "requirement_hash", "because", "base_model", "base_rank",
                      "base_source"]

# The ops that may concern every subscriber, and therefore PAGE through them.
# `prose_settle` is the hand's own continuation of a translation (GH #858): it
# reads the subscribers of one requirement, page by page.
PAGED = ("remap", "override_set", "override_clear", "model_upsert", "model_retire",
         "retranslate", "prose_settle")


def page_of(cmd):
    return as_int(cmd.get("page"), 1)


def subscriber_where(cmd):
    """The subscribers an op reads -- exactly its own, wherever it can.

    Review of the L2a strand, I-2: one unfiltered page of `subscriber_rows`
    left every row past the bound unseen, so a `remap` or a replacement did not
    reach it, a `reset` refused it, and a `subscribe` or an announcement did
    not find it and wrote it a SECOND time (the store keeps no key). So a
    subscription and a reset read their own paths exactly, a remap reads its
    tier, a translation reads the subscribers of its requirement, and the ops
    that may concern anybody read page by page from a cursor on `cell_path` --
    the order every page is read in.
    """
    op = cmd.get("op", "")
    if op == "subscribe":
        return {"cell_path": {"in": [e["cell_path"] for e in cmd.get("entries") or []]}}
    if op == "reset":
        return {"cell_path": cmd.get("cell_path", "")}
    where = {}
    if op == "remap":
        where["tier"] = cmd.get("tier", "")
    if op == "prose_settle":
        where["requirement_hash"] = cmd.get("rh", "")
    if op == "show" and cmd.get("cell_path"):
        # Below the path, never beside it (review of fix round 1, m-2): `-`
        # sorts before `/`, so `>= <path>` let `<path>-1/...` fill the page
        # before `<path>/...` came. Every path below starts with `<path>/`,
        # and those follow `<path>/` without a gap; the path itself is a probe
        # of its own (`extra_reads`).
        where["cell_path"] = {"gt": cmd["cell_path"].rstrip("/") + "/"}
    if op in PAGED and cmd.get("cursor"):
        where["cell_path"] = {"gt": cmd["cursor"]}
    return where


def extra_reads(cmd):
    """The reads one op adds to its bundle after the four, in a fixed order.

    A function of the command alone, so the phase that reads the answer finds
    each result at the index the phase that asked put it.
    """
    op = cmd.get("op", "")
    out = []
    if op == "override_set" and cmd.get("scope") == "target" and page_of(cmd) == 1:
        # `no_subscriber` is decided against the whole table and not against
        # one page of it: the path itself, and the first path below it.
        m = cmd.get("match", "").rstrip("/")
        out.append(call("select", table="subscribers", columns=["cell_path"],
                        where={"cell_path": m}, limit=1))
        out.append(call("select", table="subscribers", columns=["cell_path"],
                        where={"cell_path": {"gt": m + "/"}},
                        order_by=[{"col": "cell_path", "dir": "asc"}], limit=1))
    if op == "show" and cmd.get("cell_path"):
        out.append(call("select", table="subscribers", columns=SUBSCRIBER_COLUMNS,
                        where={"cell_path": cmd["cell_path"].rstrip("/")}, limit=1))
    if op in ("model_upsert", "model_retire"):
        # The row as it stands, retired or not: an upsert merges into it, a
        # retirement needs it to exist. Every page reads it, because every
        # page lays the change over its own catalogue read.
        out.append(call("select", table="models", columns=MODEL_COLUMNS,
                        where={"model_id": cmd.get("model_id", "")}, limit=1))
    if op == "prose_settle" and page_of(cmd) == 1:
        # Is this very (requirement, catalogue) already answered? Two
        # translations of one pair in flight together store the first.
        out.append(call("select", table="translations",
                        columns=["requirement_hash", "catalogue_hash", "model_id"],
                        where={"requirement_hash": cmd.get("rh", ""),
                               "catalogue_hash": cmd.get("ch", "")}, limit=1))
    return out


TRANSLATION_COLUMNS = ["requirement_hash", "catalogue_hash", "model_id", "reason", "at"]

# Reads per requirement of a page (`translation_reads`), in this order.
PER_REQUIREMENT_READS = 3


def translation_reads(cmd):
    """GH #858 -- three reads per requirement of a page, once the page knows
    them: the translation for this catalogue; the newest one of any catalogue
    whose model is ACTIVE (review of the strand, m-1: the newest row of all
    may name a retired model while an older one still fits); and whether a
    question for this very pair is open (I-1). Every tie has a literal key
    (m-2): of two rows for one pair the first stored wins."""
    probe = cmd.get("probe") or {}
    if probe.get("page") != page_of(cmd):
        return []
    ids = list(probe.get("ids") or []) or [""]
    cutoff = probe.get("cutoff") or open_cutoff()
    out = []
    for rh in probe.get("rhs") or []:
        out.append(call("select", table="translations", columns=TRANSLATION_COLUMNS,
                        where={"requirement_hash": rh, "catalogue_hash": probe.get("ch", "")},
                        order_by=[{"col": "at", "dir": "asc"},
                                  {"col": "model_id", "dir": "asc"}],
                        limit=1))
        out.append(call("select", table="translations", columns=TRANSLATION_COLUMNS,
                        where={"requirement_hash": rh, "model_id": {"in": ids}},
                        order_by=[{"col": "at", "dir": "desc"},
                                  {"col": "catalogue_hash", "dir": "asc"},
                                  {"col": "model_id", "dir": "asc"}],
                        limit=1))
        out.append(call("select", table="open_questions", columns=["claim"],
                        where={"requirement_hash": rh, "catalogue_hash": probe.get("ch", ""),
                               "at": {"gt": cutoff}},
                        limit=1))
    return out


def claim_calls(rh, ch, cid, stamp):
    """GH #858, review I-1 -- a question written down as open, in the bundle
    that also carries the op's writes. The store runs a bundle whole and one
    bundle after the other, so of two ops asking the same pair the first
    bundle finds nothing open and the second finds the first one's row: the
    read comes BEFORE this op's own insert. An open question past
    `OPEN_QUESTION_SECONDS` is removed first -- that is its expiry."""
    return [
        call("delete", table="open_questions",
             where={"requirement_hash": rh, "catalogue_hash": ch,
                    "at": {"lte": open_cutoff()}}),
        call("select", table="open_questions", columns=["claim"],
             where={"requirement_hash": rh, "catalogue_hash": ch}, limit=1),
        call("insert", table="open_questions", row={
            "requirement_hash": rh, "catalogue_hash": ch, "claim": cid, "at": stamp}),
    ]


def close_question(cid):
    """The open question of one claim, gone: answered, refused, failed, or
    not asked after all."""
    return call("delete", table="open_questions", where={"claim": cid})


def read_world(cmd):
    """Everything an op resolves against, in ONE bundle: the four tables, the
    op's own probes, and -- on the pass that knows them -- the translations of
    the requirements on this page."""
    calls = [
        call("select", table="models",
             columns=MODEL_COLUMNS, where={"status": "active"},
             order_by=[{"col": "model_id", "dir": "asc"}], limit=CATALOG_ROWS),
        call("select", table="tiers", columns=["tier", "model_id", "since"],
             where={"active": 1}, order_by=[{"col": "tier", "dir": "asc"}],
             limit=CATALOG_ROWS),
        call("select", table="overrides",
             columns=["id", "scope", "match", "model_id", "since", "decided_by"],
             where={"active": 1}, order_by=[{"col": "since", "dir": "asc"}],
             limit=CATALOG_ROWS),
        call("select", table="subscribers", columns=SUBSCRIBER_COLUMNS,
             where=subscriber_where(cmd),
             order_by=[{"col": "cell_path", "dir": "asc"}], limit=SUBSCRIBER_ROWS)]
    calls += extra_reads(cmd)
    calls += translation_reads(cmd)
    return store_bundle("world", {"cmd": cmd}, calls)


def model_spec(raw):
    """(row fields, error) of a `model_upsert` command's `model` object."""
    if not isinstance(raw, dict):
        return None, "incomplete_command"
    out = {}
    for k, v in raw.items():
        if k == "model_id":
            continue
        want = MODEL_FIELDS.get(k)
        if want is None:
            return None, "unknown_model_field"
        if want is int and (isinstance(v, bool) or not isinstance(v, int) or v < 0):
            return None, "invalid_model_field"
        if want is not int and not isinstance(v, want):
            return None, "invalid_model_field"
        if k == "status" and v not in MODEL_STATUSES:
            return None, "invalid_model_field"
        if k == "prompt" and len(v.encode("utf-8")) > MODEL_PROMPT_MAX_BYTES:
            return None, "invalid_model_field"
        if k == "strengths" and len(v.encode("utf-8")) > STRENGTHS_MAX_BYTES:
            return None, "invalid_model_field"
        out[k] = v
    return out, ""


def model_id_ok(mid):
    """One token of a provider's list, at most `MODEL_ID_MAX_CHARS` long."""
    return len(mid) <= MODEL_ID_MAX_CHARS and MODEL_ID_FORM.fullmatch(mid) is not None


def merged_model(cmd, existing):
    """The row an upsert writes: the stored row, the command's fields over it,
    and the defaults a new row needs. `status` defaults to active."""
    row = {"model_id": cmd["model_id"], "provider": "", "base_url": "", "wire_dialect": "",
           "context_window": 0, "cost_in": 0, "cost_out": 0, "caps": {}, "traits": {},
           "strengths": "", "status": "active", "note": "", "package": {}, "prompt": ""}
    for k in MODEL_FIELDS:
        if existing and existing.get(k) is not None:
            v = existing.get(k)
            row[k] = as_obj(v) if MODEL_FIELDS[k] is dict else v
    row.update(cmd.get("model") or {})
    return row


def overlay_catalogue(cmd, world, existing):
    """Lay a catalogue op over this page's read, in memory, on every page and
    every pass -- so each resolves against the statement whether or not the
    store has applied the write yet."""
    op = cmd.get("op", "")
    mid = cmd.get("model_id", "")
    if op == "model_upsert":
        row = merged_model(cmd, existing)
        if row["status"] == "active":
            world["models"][mid] = row
        else:
            world["models"].pop(mid, None)
    elif op == "model_retire":
        world["models"].pop(mid, None)

            "because": ("" if str(s.get("rank") or "") != "prose"

def subscribe_rows(cmd, by_path, stamp):
    """(rows to settle, writes) of a subscription or an announcement. Pure in
    the store's sense: the writes are returned, and the caller decides whether
    this pass writes at all."""
    fresh, writes = [], []
    operator = not cmd.get("announce")
    for p in cmd.get("outside") or []:
        writes.append(journal_call(cmd, p, "hand_announce_outside_generation", "", ""))
    for p in cmd.get("too_long") or []:
        writes.append(journal_call(cmd, p, "hand_requirement_too_long", "", ""))
    for e in cmd.get("entries") or []:
        path, start = e["cell_path"], e["start_model"]
        have = by_path.get(path)
        change = {}
        held = str(have.get("start_model") or "") if have else ""
        # GH #858, review rev-L2b2 m-2: an ANNOUNCEMENT with no start value says
        # nothing about it and clears none. meclaw-os announces its judge with
        # an empty one (the shell substitutes nothing), so a start value an
        # operator stated with `subscribe` has to survive every later receipt.
        if (not have or held != start) and (start or operator or not held):
            change["start_model"] = start
        # GH #858: a requirement is stated or not; an entry that does not
        # carry the key says nothing about it and changes nothing.
        if "requirement" in e:
            req = e["requirement"]
            if not have or str(have.get("requirement") or "") != req:
                change["requirement"] = req
                change["requirement_hash"] = requirement_hash(req)
        # Tier and pin are OPERATOR statements: an announcement from the
        # tree knows the start value and the requirement, and never moves them.
        if operator and cmd.get("pinned") is not None:
            pin = 1 if as_int(cmd.get("pinned"), 0) == 1 else 0
            if not have or as_int(have.get("pinned"), 0) != pin:
                change["pinned"] = pin
        if operator and cmd.get("tier") and (not have or str(have.get("tier") or "") != cmd["tier"]):
            change["tier"] = cmd["tier"]
        if have and not change:
            continue  # already known, and known the same way: nothing to do
        if have:
            writes.append(call("update", table="subscribers", set=change,
                               where={"cell_path": path}))
            row = dict(have)
            row.update(change)
        else:
            req = change.get("requirement", "")
            row = {"cell_path": path, "start_model": start,
                   "tier": change.get("tier", ""), "pinned": change.get("pinned", 0),
                   "wired_at": stamp, "package_hash": "", "model_id": start,
                   "rank": "start", "reason": "start_value", "since": stamp,
                   "requirement": req, "requirement_hash": requirement_hash(req),
                   "because": "", "base_model": "", "base_rank": "", "base_source": ""}
            # Delete, then insert (the store convention for a row that must
            # exist once): two announcements of the same brain in flight
            # together both read "unknown", and without the delete the
            # second one would leave a second row (review I-2).
            writes.append(call("delete", table="subscribers",
                               where={"cell_path": path}))
            writes.append(call("insert", table="subscribers", row=row))
        writes.append(journal_call(cmd, path, "hand_subscribed", "start", "", start))
        fresh.append(row)
    return fresh, writes


def prose_of(cmd, results, base, world):
    """GH #858 -- the translation each requirement of this page resolves to.

    Returns ({rh: {model_id, reason}}, {rh: answered for THIS catalogue},
    {rh: a question for this catalogue is open}).
    The translation for the current catalogue wins; without one the newest of
    any catalogue holds -- the last resolution stays while a new question is
    unanswered or its answer was refused. A translation whose model is not
    active is none: a retired model is never a result.
    """
    probe = cmd.get("probe") or {}
    prose, answered, pending = {}, {}, {}
    if probe.get("page") != page_of(cmd):
        return prose, answered, pending
    ch_now = catalogue_hash(world)
    fresh = cmd.get("stored") or {}

    def at(k):
        return results[k] if k < len(results) else []

    for i, rh in enumerate(probe.get("rhs") or []):
        k = base + PER_REQUIREMENT_READS * i
        exact = first_row(at(k))
        latest = first_row(at(k + 1))
        pending[rh] = first_row(at(k + 2)) is not None
        if exact and str(exact.get("catalogue_hash") or "") != ch_now:
            exact = None
        if latest and str(latest.get("catalogue_hash") or "") == ch_now and not exact:
            exact = latest
        new = fresh if fresh.get("requirement_hash") == rh else None
        if new and new.get("catalogue_hash") == ch_now and not exact:
            exact = new
        answered[rh] = exact is not None
        for pick in (exact, new, latest):
            if pick and str(pick.get("model_id") or "") in world["models"]:
                prose[rh] = {"model_id": str(pick.get("model_id") or ""),
                             "reason": one_line(pick.get("reason"), REASON_MAX_CHARS)}
                break
    return prose, answered, pending


def ask_translation(rh, ch, requirement, world, cid):
    """One question to the translator: a requirement against this catalogue.

    Its answer comes back to this cell as phase `translated`; nothing waits for
    it, and nothing resolves differently until it is a row. `cid` is the claim
    of the open question, closed with the answer.
    """
    lines = [json.dumps(r, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False) for r in catalogue_rows(world)]
    text = ("What the cell needs:\n" + requirement
            + "\n\nThe catalogue, one model per line:\n" + "\n".join(lines))
    return emit("translate", "translated",
                {"rh": rh, "ch": ch, "requirement": requirement, "cid": cid},
                None, {"system": {"instructions": {"text": TRANSLATOR_INSTRUCTIONS}},
                       "messages": [{"origin": "user", "type": "text", "text": text}]})


def parse_answer(text):
    """{model_id, reason} from the translator's text, or None.

    Strict: ONE JSON object, optionally inside a single code fence, with a
    non-empty `model_id` string. Whether the id is in the catalogue is decided
    against the catalogue, later, not here.
    """
    t = (text or "").strip()
    if t.startswith("```"):
        t = t[3:]
        if t.lower().startswith("json"):
            t = t[4:]
        if t.rstrip().endswith("```"):
            t = t.rstrip()[:-3]
        t = t.strip()
    try:
        o = json.loads(t)
    except Exception:
        return None
    if not isinstance(o, dict):
        return None
    mid = o.get("model_id")
    reason = o.get("reason")
    if not isinstance(mid, str) or not mid.strip():
        return None
    return {"model_id": mid.strip(), "reason": one_line(reason, REASON_MAX_CHARS)}

        cmd["requirement"] = req
    incomplete = (
        (op == "remap" and (not cmd["tier"] or not cmd["model_id"]))
        or (op == "override_set" and (cmd["scope"] not in ("global", "target")
                                      or not cmd["match"].strip() or not cmd["model_id"]))
        or (op == "override_clear" and not cmd["id"])
        or (op == "reset" and not cmd["cell_path"])
        or (op == "model_retire" and not cmd["model_id"])
        or (op == "subscribe" and (not cmd["cell_path"]
                                   or not (cmd["start_model"] or cmd.get("requirement")))))
    if incomplete:
        sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(refuse(cmd, "incomplete_command")))
        sys.exit(0)
    if op == "subscribe":
        entry = {"cell_path": cmd["cell_path"], "start_model": cmd["start_model"]}
        if "requirement" in cmd:
            entry["requirement"] = cmd["requirement"]
        cmd["entries"] = [entry]
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps([read_world(cmd)]))
    sys.exit(0)

if phase == "translated":
    # GH #858 -- the translator answered, or failed to. Either way this is the
    # end of ITS part: an answer becomes a candidate row that is checked
    # against the catalogue on the next read, a failure becomes a journal
    # line, and in both cases every subscriber keeps what it resolved to until
    # a row says otherwise.
    rh = str(carry.get("rh") or "")
    ch = str(carry.get("ch") or "")
    cid = str(carry.get("cid") or "")
    note = {"op": "translate", "tier": "", "model_id": "", "internal": True}
    text = ""
    for m in reversed(d.get("messages") or []):
        if m.get("origin") == "assistant" and m.get("type") == "text":
            text = str(m.get("text") or "")
            break
    finish = str(hop.get("finish_reason") or "")
    answer = parse_answer(text) if finish == "stop" else None
    if answer is None:
        why = "translation_failed" if finish != "stop" else "translation_unreadable"
        # The question is closed with the failure: the next trigger asks again.
        sys.stdout.write(json.dumps([store_bundle("written", None, [
            journal_call(note, "", why, "prose", rh, ""), close_question(cid)])]))
        sys.exit(0)
    cmd = {"op": "prose_settle", "internal": True, "actor": "translator", "tier": "",
           "model_id": answer["model_id"], "rh": rh, "ch": ch, "cid": cid,
           "answer": answer, "page": 1}
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps([read_world(cmd)]))
    sys.exit(0)

if phase == "claimed":
    # GH #858, review I-1 -- the store's echo of a bundle that wrote an op's
    # changes and claimed its open questions. Per claim it holds three results
    # (expired removed, the open question found BEFORE this claim, the claim),
    # then the catalogue as it stands after the op's own writes. A question
    # somebody else holds open is not asked again. The rest are asked, with
    # the catalogue of this very read -- also one whose catalogue moved since
    # the op read it (review rev2-L2b1, m-A): the op that moved it may never
    # have seen this subscriber (a `subscribe` of a new cell racing a
    # `model_upsert` that read its page before the row existed), and leaving
    # the question to it left the requirement unasked until the next trigger.
    # The claim moves with the question; should the mover have asked the same
    # pair, the second answer is journalled `translation_duplicate`.
    results = results_of(d)
    n = as_int(carry.get("n"), 0)
    claims = carry.get("claims") or []
    k = n + 3 * len(claims)
    cat = results[k] if k < len(results) else []
    world = {"models": {str(r.get("model_id") or ""): r for r in cat
                        if isinstance(r, dict) and r.get("model_id")}}
    ch_now = catalogue_hash(world)
    out, dropped = [], []
    for i, c in enumerate(claims):
        cid = str(c.get("cid") or "")
        before = results[n + 3 * i + 1] if n + 3 * i + 1 < len(results) else []
        if first_row(before) is not None or not world["models"]:
            # Not asked here, so not held open by this claim either.
            dropped.append(close_question(cid))
            continue
        if str(c.get("ch") or "") != ch_now:
            dropped.append(call("update", table="open_questions",
                                set={"catalogue_hash": ch_now}, where={"claim": cid}))
        # Asked: the claim stays open until the answer (or the failure)
        # closes it, or until it expires.
        out.append(ask_translation(str(c.get("rh") or ""), ch_now,
                                   str(c.get("requirement") or ""), world, cid))
    if dropped:
        out.append(store_bundle("written", None, dropped))
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(out))
    sys.exit(0)

if phase == "world":
    cmd = carry.get("cmd") or {}
    results = results_of(d)
    world = world_of(results)
    op = cmd.get("op", "")
    subs = world["subs"]
    # A page that came back FULL may have a next one; `subs` is what this page
    # holds, in `cell_path` order, so its last path is the next cursor.
    full = len(subs) >= SUBSCRIBER_ROWS
    by_path = {str(s.get("cell_path") or ""): s for s in subs}
    writes, out = [], []
    page = page_of(cmd)
    first = page == 1
    stamp = cmd.get("stamp") or now()
    decided = cmd.get("actor", "")
    n_extra = len(extra_reads(cmd))
    extras = (results + [[]] * (4 + n_extra))[4:4 + n_extra]

    if op == "show":
        narrow = str(cmd.get("cell_path") or "").rstrip("/")
        if narrow:
            itself = [r for r in (extras[0] if extras else []) if isinstance(r, dict)]
            below = [s for s in subs if under(str(s.get("cell_path") or ""), narrow)]
            rows = [view(s) for s in itself + below]
            # The page ran past the paths below: nothing was cut.
            cut = full and len(below) == len(subs)
        else:
            rows = [view(s) for s in subs]
            cut = full
        answer = {"op": "show", "cells": rows,
                  # One page, and it says when it is one: raise
                  # `subscriber_rows`, or narrow with `cell_path`.
                  "truncated": cut,
                  "overrides": [{"id": str(o.get("id") or ""), "scope": o.get("scope"),
                                 "match": o.get("match"), "model_id": o.get("model_id"),
                                 "since": o.get("since"), "decided_by": o.get("decided_by")}
                                for o in world["overrides"]],
                  "precedence": list(RANKS),
                  # What a cell RUNS is not in any table here: a brain answers a
                  # push with nothing, and one that refused it (a `base_url`
                  # outside its `base_url_allow`, say) says so on its own error
                  # lane and keeps its previous params. So the view says what
                  # was resolved and SENT, and says that it is only that.
                  "view": "model_id is what the registry resolved and last sent to each "
                          "cell; a push the cell refused shows on that cell's error lane, "
                          "and the cell keeps running its previous params"}
        sys.stdout.write(json.dumps([emit("answer", "", None,
                                          {"outcome": "shown", "reason_code": "shown"},
                                          {"messages": [{"origin": "tool",
                                                         "type": "tool_result",
                                                         "id": cmd.get("call_id", ""),
                                                         "text": json.dumps(answer)}]})]))
        sys.exit(0)

    # --- refusals: decided on the first page, before anything is written ----
    existing = first_row(extras[0]) if op in ("model_upsert", "model_retire") and extras else None
    if first and op == "model_retire" and (
            not existing or str(existing.get("status") or "") != "active"):
        sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(refuse(cmd, "unknown_model")))
        sys.exit(0)
    overlay_catalogue(cmd, world, existing)

    needs_model = op in ("remap", "override_set")
    if first and needs_model and cmd.get("model_id") not in world["models"]:
        # An index or a replacement may only point at a row that exists and is
        # active: pointing at a name the catalogue does not carry would move
        # every reached subscriber onto something nobody described.
        sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(refuse(cmd, "unknown_model")))
        sys.exit(0)
    if first and op == "override_set" and cmd.get("scope") == "target" and not any(
            under(str(r.get("cell_path") or ""), cmd["match"])
            for rows in extras for r in rows if isinstance(r, dict)):
        sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(refuse(cmd, "no_subscriber")))
        sys.exit(0)
    if first and op == "override_clear" and not any(
            str(o.get("id") or "") == cmd["id"] for o in world["overrides"]):
        sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(refuse(cmd, "unknown_override")))
        sys.exit(0)
    if op == "reset" and not by_path.get(cmd["cell_path"]):
        sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(refuse(cmd, "no_subscriber")))
        sys.exit(0)
    if first and op == "prose_settle":
        # The translator's answer is checked HERE, against the catalogue as it
        # stands: a model it does not carry as active is no answer (GH #858).
        # Nothing is stored, nothing moves, one journal line says why.
        answer = cmd.get("answer") or {}
        if first_row(extras[0] if extras else []):
            sys.stdout.write(json.dumps([store_bundle("written", None, [
                journal_call(cmd, "", "translation_duplicate", "prose", cmd.get("rh", ""),
                             answer.get("model_id", "")),
                close_question(cmd.get("cid", ""))])]))
            sys.exit(0)
        if answer.get("model_id") not in world["models"]:
            sys.stdout.write(json.dumps([store_bundle("written", None, [
                journal_call(cmd, "", "translation_outside_catalogue", "prose",
                             cmd.get("rh", ""), answer.get("model_id", "")),
                close_question(cmd.get("cid", ""))])]))
            sys.exit(0)

    # --- which subscribers this page settles --------------------------------
    if op == "subscribe":
        rows, sub_writes = subscribe_rows(cmd, by_path, stamp)
    elif op == "reset":
        rows, sub_writes = [by_path[cmd["cell_path"]]], []
    else:
        rows, sub_writes = subs, []

    # --- GH #858: a page with requirements reads their translations first ---
    # The requirements are known only once the page is read, and the
    # catalogue hash only once the catalogue is -- so such a page is read a
    # second time, with two translation reads per requirement in the same
    # bundle. Nothing is written before that second pass.
    rhs = sorted({str(r.get("requirement_hash") or "") for r in rows} - {""})
    probe = cmd.get("probe") or {}
    if rhs and probe.get("page") != page:
        again = dict(cmd, probe={"page": page, "ch": catalogue_hash(world), "rhs": rhs,
                                 "ids": sorted(world["models"]), "cutoff": open_cutoff()})
        sys.stdout.write(json.dumps([read_world(again)]))
        sys.exit(0)
    if first and op == "prose_settle":
        answer = cmd.get("answer") or {}
        cmd["stored"] = {"requirement_hash": cmd.get("rh", ""),
                         "catalogue_hash": cmd.get("ch", ""),
                         "model_id": answer.get("model_id", ""),
                         "reason": answer.get("reason", ""), "at": stamp}
    world["prose"], answered, pending = prose_of(cmd, results, 4 + n_extra, world)
    writes += sub_writes

    # --- the paged ops: the change is written once, on the first page, and
    # laid over every page's world in memory -- so each page resolves against
    # the same statement whether or not the store has applied the write yet.
    if op in PAGED and first:
        cmd["stamp"] = stamp
        if op == "remap":
            writes.append(call("update", table="tiers", set={"active": 0},
                               where={"tier": cmd["tier"]}))
            writes.append(call("insert", table="tiers", row={
                "tier": cmd["tier"], "model_id": cmd["model_id"], "since": stamp,
                "decided_by": decided, "active": 1}))
        elif op == "override_set":
            row = {"id": uuid.uuid4().hex[:16], "scope": cmd["scope"],
                   "match": cmd["match"], "model_id": cmd["model_id"], "since": stamp,
                   "decided_by": decided, "active": 1}
            cmd["row"] = row
            # Supersede, never overwrite: the replacement this one takes over
            # from stays readable, inactive, with the time it stopped.
            writes.append(call("update", table="overrides", set={"active": 0},
                               where={"scope": cmd["scope"], "match": cmd["match"],
                                      "active": 1}))
            writes.append(call("insert", table="overrides", row=row))
        elif op == "override_clear":
            writes.append(call("update", table="overrides", set={"active": 0},
                               where={"id": cmd["id"]}))
        elif op == "model_upsert":
            # Delete, then insert: one row per model id, whatever was there.
            writes.append(call("delete", table="models", where={"model_id": cmd["model_id"]}))
            writes.append(call("insert", table="models", row=merged_model(cmd, existing)))
            writes.append(journal_call(cmd, "", "hand_model_upsert", "", ""))
        elif op == "model_retire":
            writes.append(call("update", table="models", set={"status": "retired"},
                               where={"model_id": cmd["model_id"]}))
            writes.append(journal_call(cmd, "", "hand_model_retire", "", ""))
        elif op == "prose_settle":
            s = cmd["stored"]
            writes.append(call("insert", table="translations", row={
                "requirement_hash": s["requirement_hash"], "catalogue_hash": s["catalogue_hash"],
                "model_id": s["model_id"], "reason": s["reason"], "at": s["at"]}))
            writes.append(journal_call(cmd, "", "translation_stored", "prose", s["requirement_hash"],
                                       s["model_id"]))
            writes.append(close_question(cmd.get("cid", "")))

    touched = lambda s: False
    reason_push = {"remap": "hand_remap", "override_set": "hand_override_set",
                   "override_clear": "hand_override_clear", "reset": "hand_reset",
                   "subscribe": "hand_subscribe", "model_upsert": "hand_model_upsert",
                   "model_retire": "hand_model_retire", "retranslate": "hand_retranslate",
                   "prose_settle": "hand_prose"}.get(op, "hand_" + op)
    if op == "remap":
        world["tiers"][cmd["tier"]] = {"tier": cmd["tier"], "model_id": cmd["model_id"],
                                       "since": stamp}
        touched = lambda s: True
    elif op == "override_set":
        row = cmd["row"]
        world["overrides"] = [o for o in world["overrides"]
                              if not (o.get("scope") == row["scope"]
                                      and o.get("match") == row["match"])] + [row]
        touched = (lambda s: cmd["scope"] == "global"
                   and base_of(s, world)[0] == cmd["match"])
    elif op == "override_clear":
        world["overrides"] = [o for o in world["overrides"]
                              if str(o.get("id") or "") != cmd["id"]]
    elif op == "reset":
        mine = [o for o in world["overrides"]
                if o.get("scope") == "target" and str(o.get("match") or "") == cmd["cell_path"]]
        for o in mine:
            writes.append(call("update", table="overrides", set={"active": 0},
                               where={"id": str(o.get("id") or "")}))
        world["overrides"] = [o for o in world["overrides"] if o not in mine]
        cmd["cleared"] = len(mine)

    w, pushes, counts = settle(cmd, rows, world, reason_push, "hand_skipped_pinned", touched)
    writes += w
    out += pushes

    # --- GH #858: the questions this op leaves unanswered -------------------
    # Once per distinct requirement: `asked` rides along from page to page, so
    # a requirement a hundred subscribers share is one question. And once
    # across ops (review I-1): a question another op holds open is skipped
    # here, and the ones left are CLAIMED in this op's write bundle -- the
    # question itself goes out from the store's echo, to whichever claim came
    # first (phase `claimed`).
    claims = []
    if op in ASKING and world["models"]:
        asked = list(cmd.get("asked") or [])
        texts = {}
        for r in rows:
            rh = str(r.get("requirement_hash") or "")
            if rh and rh not in texts:
                texts[rh] = str(r.get("requirement") or "")
        ch = catalogue_hash(world)
        for rh in sorted(texts):
            if answered.get(rh) or pending.get(rh) or rh in asked or not texts[rh]:
                continue
            claims.append({"rh": rh, "ch": ch, "requirement": texts[rh],
                           "cid": uuid.uuid4().hex})
            asked.append(rh)
        cmd["asked"] = asked

    if op in PAGED:
        acc = cmd.get("acc") or {"pushed": 0, "unchanged": 0, "skipped_pinned": 0,
                                 "subscribers": 0}
        for k, v in counts.items():
            acc[k] = acc.get(k, 0) + v
        acc["subscribers"] = acc.get("subscribers", 0) + len(subs)
        if full:
            # The next page, from the last path this one held.
            nxt = dict(cmd, page=page + 1, acc=acc,
                       cursor=str(subs[-1].get("cell_path") or ""))
            out.append(read_world(nxt))
        elif not cmd.get("internal"):
            extra = dict(acc, pages=page)
            done_code = {"remap": "remapped", "override_set": "override_set",
                         "override_clear": "override_cleared",
                         "model_upsert": "model_upserted", "model_retire": "model_retired",
                         "retranslate": "retranslated"}[op]
            if op == "remap":
                extra["reason"] = cmd.get("reason", "")
            elif op == "override_set":
                extra.update(id=cmd["row"]["id"], scope=cmd["scope"], match=cmd["match"])
            elif op == "override_clear":
                extra["id"] = cmd["id"]
            if op in ASKING:
                extra["translations_asked"] = len(cmd.get("asked") or [])
            out.append(ack(cmd, "accepted", done_code, extra))
    elif op == "reset":
        out.append(ack(cmd, "accepted", "reset", dict(counts, cleared=cmd.get("cleared", 0),
                                                      cell_path=cmd["cell_path"])))
    elif op == "subscribe" and not cmd.get("announce"):
        out.append(ack(cmd, "accepted", "subscribed",
                       dict(counts, subscribed=len(rows),
                            translations_asked=len(cmd.get("asked") or []))))

    if claims:
        claim_stamp = now()
        calls = list(writes)
        for c in claims:
            calls += claim_calls(c["rh"], c["ch"], c["cid"], claim_stamp)
        calls.append(call("select", table="models", columns=MODEL_COLUMNS,
                          where={"status": "active"},
                          order_by=[{"col": "model_id", "dir": "asc"}], limit=CATALOG_ROWS))
        out.insert(0, store_bundle("claimed", {"n": len(writes), "claims": claims}, calls))
    elif writes:
        out.insert(0, store_bundle("written", None, writes))
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(out))
    sys.exit(0)

# phase "written": the store's echo of a write bundle. Terminal.
sys.stdout.write("[]")

subscriber_rows.description: Page bound of the subscriber read one op resolves: how many subscriber rows a single hop reads, resolves and may push to. An op that may concern every subscriber (`remap`, `override_set`, `override_clear`) pages on until a read comes back short, and `subscribe`, `reset` and an announcement read their own paths exactly, so it bounds the WORK of one hop, not the number of subscribers a registry may hold or reach. `show` answers one page and says `truncated` when the bound cut it.

catalog_rows.description: Page bound of the catalogue reads one op resolves against: at most this many active models, active tiers and active overrides are read per round. It bounds the WORK of one hop, not the size of the catalogue.

description.purpose: The hand of the registry, and it moves ONLY when called (GH #855). Every op reads the catalogue, the tier index, the replacements and the subscribers in ONE store bundle, resolves each subscriber it concerns by one deterministic precedence -- targeted > global > prose > tier > start value -- and pushes the resolved model package to every subscriber whose package changed: a params-only body `{system: {}, params: {model, …package…, model_prompt, $reset}}` an llm cell merges into its live params and answers with nothing. Deterministic code by construction: the path that repairs a broken model must never run through the broken model. Since 2.3.0 (GH #858) a subscriber may state a requirement in prose; the hand asks `./translate` to choose from the catalogue ONLY when no translation exists for that (requirement, catalogue) pair, checks the answer against the catalogue, stores it as a row with its reason, and from then on resolves by reading that row -- the translator never stands between a command and its push.
description.use_when: On call. An operator message or an agent tool_call names the op (`remap`, `override_set`, `override_clear`, `reset`, `subscribe`, `show`, and since 2.3.0 `model_upsert`, `model_retire`, `retranslate`); the edge into this cell MUST promote the deciding identity to `context.actor`, or every op but `show` is refused. A grown generation's announcement arrives on the same lane over an edge that stamps `context.model_generation` and the brains in `context.model_announced`, and the shell's bridge adds `context.model_announcer`; it is answered by nobody, and nothing arriving that way is ever read as a command.
description.not_in_scope: There is no trigger but the call. No timer, no probe and no incident rule: nothing in this hive reacts to an `incidents` row, and that absence is the ruling, not an omission (GH #130). It cannot verify delivery -- a push is fire-and-forget into a cell that answers nothing, so the registry knows what it SENT and never what a cell RUNS. And it can only move what a package holds: `provider`, `api_key` and the auth dimension are immutable per cell, so a model behind another credential is a rebirth, not a message.
description.emits_meaning: route update: one params-only message per subscriber whose package changed, hop.subscriber naming the cell path so the parent edge finds it and hop.rank naming the rule that chose it. route ack: accepted or rejected plus a reason_code (unknown_op, no_actor, incomplete_command, unknown_model, no_subscriber, unknown_override, unknown_model_field, invalid_model_field, requirement_too_long) and the counts pushed / unchanged / skipped_pinned / subscribers / pages, after the last page. route answer: the view `show` returns, with `truncated` when the page bound cut it. route rstore: one bundled read per page (a page with requirements is read twice, the second time with its translations), one bundled write. route translate: one question to ./translate per distinct requirement that has no translation for the current catalogue -- the requirement and the active catalogue in the body, the key in the carry; its answer comes back as phase `translated`, and is journalled translation_stored, translation_outside_catalogue, translation_duplicate, translation_failed or translation_unreadable. route error: the store refused an op, or the command was not a tool_call turn carrying JSON, or an announcement named no brain. An announcement that cannot be served is journalled, never acknowledged: no_announcer, announcer_carries_no_announcement, no_generation, and hand_announce_outside_generation per brain it named outside its generation.
description.consumes_meaning: context.lr_phase and context.lr_carry hold the command across the store round trip. context.actor is edge truth and becomes the `decided_by` of every tier row and replacement. context.model_announcer marks the announcement lane: whatever arrives with it is an announcement and never a command, whatever turn it carries. context.model_generation is the generation the announcing edge was drawn for, and only brains inside it are taken. context.model_announced carries the announced brains, stamped by the same edge; a list on hop.subscribe is never read, because a hop key survives a transit through a foreign hive. context.registry_origin 'translate' marks the translator's answer; the door into this cell clears it together with lr_phase and lr_carry, so only the internal edge from ./translate can set it.
examples: {"op":"override_set","scope":"global","match":"provider-a/model-mid","model_id":"provider-b/model-large"} -> one replacement row, and every unpinned subscriber whose base model is provider-a/model-mid gets the whole package of provider-b/model-large, with `$reset` for every package key it does not set

{"op":"remap","tier":"mid","model_id":"provider-b/model-large","reason":"provider-a degraded"} -> the tier row supersedes, every unpinned mid subscriber whose package changed gets one params message, the pinned ones get a journal line saying they were skipped
the same command with a model the catalog does not carry as active -> rejected unknown_model, nothing written but the journal line, nothing sent

the same command over an edge that promotes no actor -> rejected no_actor. Only `show`, which reads and changes nothing, needs no identity; every other op changes what other cells run, so it needs one an edge wrote
a tool_call turn over the announcement edge (context.model_announcer set), even with an actor in context -> journalled announcer_carries_no_announcement, nothing else happens

{"op":"subscribe","cell_path":"/p/brain","start_model":"<start>","requirement":"Talks with one person; fast replies, tools, a modest price."} -> the row, one question to ./translate if nobody asked it for this catalogue yet, and once the answer is a row, one push ranked `prose` with the translator's sentence in `show`

{"op":"model_upsert","model":{"model_id":"vendor/model","cost_in":10,"cost_out":50,"strengths":"fast, cheap, good with tools"}} -> one row (merged into the stored one), every subscriber resolved again, one question per distinct requirement the new catalogue has not answered; a change that only touches `package`, `prompt`, `base_url` or `note` asks nothing
